Find the derivative of [MATH: y = 3\sech{x}+\coth{x}.]
EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
[MATH: ewcommand{\arsinh}{\mathop{ m arsinh} olimits} ewcommand{\arcosh}{\mathop{ m arcosh} olimits} ewcommand{\artanh}{\mathop{ m artanh} olimits} ewcommand{\sech}{\mathop{ m sech} olimits} ewcommand{\csch}{\mathop{ m csch} olimits} ewcommand{\coth}{\mathop{ m coth} olimits} ewcommand{\arsech}{\mathop{ m arsech} olimits} ewcommand{\arcsch}{\mathop{ m arcsch} olimits} ewcommand{\arcoth}{\mathop{ m arcoth} olimits}]

First, we recall the results for the derivatives of the basic reciprocal hyperbolic functions: [MATH: ( \sech x )' = -\sech x anh x, \quad ( \csch x )' = -\csch x \coth x, \quad ( \coth x )' = -\csch^2 x]

Differentiating the given function using these results and the rules of differentiation, we get [MATH: (dy)/(dx)|= (d)/(dx)(3sech x + \coth x); = 3(d)/(dx)(sech x) + (d)/(dx)(\coth x); = 3(− sech x anh x) + (− csch^{2} x); = − 3sech x anh x − csch^{2} x.]

items.title: Differentiating Reciprocal Hyperbolic Functions Using the Chain Rule

Find the derivative of [MATH: f(x) =\coth(5x - 2).]
EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
[MATH: ewcommand{\arsinh}{\mathop{ m arsinh} olimits} ewcommand{\arcosh}{\mathop{ m arcosh} olimits} ewcommand{\artanh}{\mathop{ m artanh} olimits} ewcommand{\sech}{\mathop{ m sech} olimits} ewcommand{\csch}{\mathop{ m csch} olimits} ewcommand{\coth}{\mathop{ m coth} olimits} ewcommand{\arsech}{\mathop{ m arsech} olimits} ewcommand{\arcsch}{\mathop{ m arcsch} olimits} ewcommand{\arcoth}{\mathop{ m arcoth} olimits}]

First, we express [MATH: f(x)] as a composite function:

[MATH: f =\coth{g}, \qquad g = 5x - 2]

The chain rule states that [MATH: \dfrac { extrm{d}f} { extrm{d}x} = \dfrac { extrm{d}f} { extrm{d}g} \cdot \dfrac { extrm{d}g} { extrm{d}x}.]

Differentiating, we have [MATH: \dfrac { extrm{d}f} { extrm{d}g} = -\csch^2{g},]

and [MATH: \dfrac { extrm{d}g} { extrm{d}x} = 5.]

Finally, multiplying the two results together and substituting for [MATH: g] gives [MATH: (df)/(dx)|= − csch^{2} g ⋅ 5; = − 5csch^{2} g; = − 5csch^{2} (5x − 2).]

Find the derivative of [MATH: f(x) = x^2\coth{x}.]
EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
[MATH: ewcommand{\arsinh}{\mathop{ m arsinh} olimits} ewcommand{\arcosh}{\mathop{ m arcosh} olimits} ewcommand{\artanh}{\mathop{ m artanh} olimits} ewcommand{\sech}{\mathop{ m sech} olimits} ewcommand{\csch}{\mathop{ m csch} olimits} ewcommand{\coth}{\mathop{ m coth} olimits} ewcommand{\arsech}{\mathop{ m arsech} olimits} ewcommand{\arcsch}{\mathop{ m arcsch} olimits} ewcommand{\arcoth}{\mathop{ m arcoth} olimits}]

Here, we have the product of two functions [MATH: u(x) = x^2] and [MATH: v(x) = \coth{x}.] So, we apply the product rule: [MATH: f^{′}(x)|= (x^{2})^{′} ⋅ \coth x + x^{2} ⋅ (\coth x)^{′}; = 2x ⋅ \coth x + x^{2} ⋅ (− csch^{2} x); = x(2\coth x − xcsch^{2} x)]

Find the derivative of [MATH: f(x) = \dfrac{\sech{x}}{4x}.]
EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
[MATH: ewcommand{\arsinh}{\mathop{ m arsinh} olimits} ewcommand{\arcosh}{\mathop{ m arcosh} olimits} ewcommand{\artanh}{\mathop{ m artanh} olimits} ewcommand{\sech}{\mathop{ m sech} olimits} ewcommand{\csch}{\mathop{ m csch} olimits} ewcommand{\coth}{\mathop{ m coth} olimits} ewcommand{\arsech}{\mathop{ m arsech} olimits} ewcommand{\arcsch}{\mathop{ m arcsch} olimits} ewcommand{\arcoth}{\mathop{ m arcoth} olimits}]

In this case, the expression for [MATH: f(x)] is a quotient [MATH: \dfrac{u(x)}{v(x)}] with [MATH: u(x) = \sech{x}] and [MATH: v(x) = 4x.]

Therefore, we apply the quotient rule as follows: [MATH: f^{′}(x)|= (u^{′}(x) ⋅ v(x) − u(x) ⋅ v^{′}(x))/([v(x)]^{2}); = ((sech x)^{′} ⋅ (4x) − sech x ⋅ (4x)^{′})/((4x)^{2}); = ((− sech x anh x) ⋅ (4x) − sech x ⋅ 4)/(16x^{2}); = − (4sech x(x anh x + 1))/(16x^{2}); = − (sech x(x anh x + 1))/(4x^{2})]
